audit.whatIsWrong: Four rows of the level chart disagreed across the two layers. Full phases[1..4].side all said 'Skill' while content win[1..4] all said 'Anivia'. The page answered 'who wins Level 2/3/4-5/6' twice, differently.
audit.why: The packet levelChart says Anivia for rows 0-4, and the content layer agrees. Anivia's Flash Frost is 1075 to Breath of Light's 750, Frostbite is a 4s cooldown that doubles on anything Flash Frost chilled, and a formed Glacial Storm doubles it too — she owns the ground through level 6. 'Skill' was the outlier.
audit.corrected: phases[1..4].side move to 'Anivia', matching win[1..4]. Because the side moved, the four whys are rewritten in the same proposal to argue for Anivia rather than describing the owner's farming plan, and phases[1..3].rating move from 5/10 to 6/10 to match row 0, which is already Anivia at 6/10. phases[4] was already 6/10.
sources: enemyKit Q range 1075 / E cd 4 / E doubling text

audit.whatIsWrong: The late-game spike was described as a 'global Comet' and a 'global ultimate'. Neither exists.
audit.why: Falling Star / The Skies Descend is 1250 range, not global, and there is no Comet in the reworked kit. Only Astral Flight (1500) gives map reach.
audit.corrected: whys[6], spikes[3] and content late rewritten around the beam, The Skies Descend and the stardust curve.

audit.whatIsWrong: The single most important interaction in this matchup was absent: Astral Flight flies over terrain, so Crystallize does not wall Aurelion Sol off. The page instead told the player Crystallize 'can wall you away from minions or cut off your escape entirely'.
audit.why: Riot's W text for Aurelion Sol: 'flies over terrain in a targeted direction'. Riot's Crystallize text: 'an impassable wall of ice to block all movement'. From level 4 the wall is a problem for his team, not for him — and Crystallize is a flat 17s while Astral Flight is 22s at rank 1, so the trade of cooldowns is close to even.
audit.corrected: Stated in report[5].t, dosFull[2].d, breakdown.cooldowns, breakdown.carry, ahead, content early, mid and late.

audit.whatIsWrong: Frostbite's doubling condition was described only vaguely ('her E never doubles') and its second trigger was never mentioned at all.
audit.why: Riot's E text: damage doubles if the target was recently hit by Flash Frost OR damaged by a fully formed Glacial Storm. So there are two ways to eat a doubled Frostbite, and the second one is standing in her ultimate — which a channelling Aurelion Sol does by default.
audit.corrected: Both triggers named in phases[4].why and content mid.

audit.whatIsWrong: Flash Frost cancelling Aurelion Sol's channels was never stated, despite being the reason his pattern does not work here.
audit.why: Breath of Light and Astral Flight both carry the interruptible-channel flag, and Flash Frost's explosion stuns. At 1075 range she cancels either one without stepping forward.
audit.corrected: Stated in tradeBad, dontsFull[2].d and report[5].t.

audit.why: Flash Frost 11s at rank 1, Crystallize a flat 17s, Frostbite 4s, Falling Star 120s at rank 1. The 4s on Frostbite in particular changes the advice: there is no window where her E is unavailable, only windows where it is not doubled.
audit.corrected: Rewritten with the Flash Frost, Crystallize and Falling Star numbers.

audit.whatIsWrong: Copy-paste bleed: dosFull[1].d ('Farm the back line with E executes') was the tradeGood string and dontsFull[2].d ('Fly W into her cooldown-loaded face') was the tradeBad string.
audit.why: Both bodies now explain their own titles.
audit.corrected: dosFull[1].d rewritten around the black hole's 12s and 90 mana; dontsFull[2].d around Flash Frost cancelling the flight from 1075.

audit.whatIsWrong: Anivia is female (champ-gender.js) and the full layer called her he/his in tldr, winCon, tradeGood, tradeBad, phases[1].why, phases[3].why, phases[4].why, breakdown.wave, dosFull[2].t, dontsFull[1].t, dontsFull[2].t, report[0], report[1], report[3], report[4] and report[11].

audit.whatIsWrong: Mechanical lint pass (tools/matchup-lint.js) over aurelionsol_mid: female enemies referred to as he/him/his in prose fields, breakdown.cooldowns fields containing no cooldown number, Do/Don't bodies that were the generic tradeGood/tradeBad string pasted under an unrelated title, "doubles" magnitude claims with no number, and report[4].t still holding the pre-audit template while breakdown.wave had been rewritten.
audit.why: Pronouns checked against champ-data/champ-gender.js; every flagged pronoun refers to the enemy laner, none to a jungler, so there are no false positives in this set. Cooldowns and ranges taken from champ-data/_kits/. report[4].t is the report mirror of breakdown.wave and had drifted out of sync on 15 matchups.

edits.before: She continues to control space with wall placement and long-range poke, and her egg form means your all-in math always has to double — kill her body, then kill the egg before it hatches. edits.before: Once your first core item lands, your Q-W burst finally threatens to kill through both her HP bar and the Rebirth egg in a single combo, flipping the damage race. notes: The chart fix here is the big one: four rows (Level 2, Level 3, Levels 4-5, Level 6) said 'Skill' in the full layer and 'Anivia' in the content layer, so the page argued with itself four times in one table. I moved the sides to Anivia to match the packet and the content layer, rewrote all four whys in the same proposal so the sentence now argues for Anivia, and lifted three ratings from 5/10 to 6/10 to match row 0's existing Anivia/6-10. If the user disagrees with the rating scale I inferred, those three are the only guessed values in this file and can be reverted independently — the sides and whys stand on the packet. Best mechanical find: Crystallize does NOT wall off Aurelion Sol from level 4 onward, because Astral Flight explicitly flies over terrain. The page said the opposite ('cut off your escape entirely'), which is advice that costs the player the lane. Data note carried from the other files: the derived 'terrain: creates terrain' flag on Astral Flight contradicts Riot's description and is misfiring; here it happens to matter, because the true behaviour (flying over terrain) is the interaction. Unverified and left alone: whether Falling Star can be cast during Astral Flight to land while airborne; whether Flash Frost's chill or its explosion is what arms the Frostbite doubling (Riot says 'recently hit by Flash Frost', which I quoted rather than interpreted); tenacity/QSS on either stun.
